templates.title: Employee Restrictive Covenant Agreement
templates.summary: Alaska-specific employee restrictive covenant agreement built for Alaska's pure common-law reasonableness regime: there is no general Alaska non-compete statute, so every post-employment restraint stands or falls on Alaska Supreme Court case law — non-competition agreements are strictly construed and weighed against the common-law reasonableness factors (reasonably necessary to protect a legitimate business interest and no broader than needed). It provides confidentiality and trade-secret protection alongside the Alaska Uniform Trade Secrets Act (AS 45.50.910–.945), customer and employee non-solicitation, an optional customer non-dealing covenant scoped to the customers and information the employer procured at its own expense, an optional non-compete drawn to the reasonable-necessity gate, optional non-investment, sale-of-business public-injury weighing for covenants tied to a business sale, and a reasonable-alteration posture that the drafting does not rely on — judicial rescue of an overbroad covenant is available only to an employer that carries the burden of proving good-faith drafting, with willful overreach forfeiting alteration. Drafted as a starting point for licensed counsel review. (OpenAgreements version 0.1.0, marked experimental by its authors.)

templates.title: Employee Restrictive Covenant Agreement
templates.summary: Alabama-specific employee restrictive covenant agreement built for the Alabama Restrictive Covenant Act, Ala. Code section 8-1-190 et seq.: confidentiality and trade-secret protection, a current-customer non-solicitation, an employee no-hire covenant confined to uniquely essential workers, and an optional non-compete drawn to the section 8-1-190(b)(4) employee exception. Recites the void-by-default rule and its six safe-harbor categories, ties each covenant to a section 8-1-191 protectable interest, keeps durations within the statutory presumptions (two years employee non-compete, eighteen months current-customer non-solicit), confirms the section 8-1-192 all-parties signature and adequate-consideration formalities, avoids execution before the employment relationship exists, carves out the section 8-1-196 professional exemption, treats reformation as reaching only duration, and applies Alabama's fundamental-policy conflicts rule. Drafted as a starting point for licensed counsel review. (OpenAgreements version 0.1.0, marked experimental by its authors.)

templates.title: Employee Restrictive Covenant Agreement
templates.summary: Arkansas-specific employee restrictive covenant agreement built for Ark. Code Ann. section 4-75-101: confidentiality and trade-secret protection, employee and customer non-solicitation, a non-dealing covenant, and an optional non-compete drawn to the statutory protectable-interest and time-and-scope test. Recites the statutory categories of protectable business interest, keeps durations within the two-year presumptively-reasonable window, relies on the continued-employment consideration rule, voids any practice restriction on a physician under the 2025 amendment, flags the Title 17, Subtitle 3 licensed-professional exclusion, and acknowledges the mandatory judicial reformation remedy. Drafted as a starting point for licensed counsel review. (OpenAgreements version 0.1.0, marked experimental by its authors.)

templates.title: Employee Restrictive Covenant Agreement
templates.summary: Arizona-specific employee restrictive covenant agreement built for Arizona's common-law reasonableness regime: there is no general Arizona non-compete statute, so every post-employment restraint stands or falls on Arizona's reasonableness test — a restriction is unreasonable and will not be enforced if it is greater than necessary to protect the employer's legitimate interest, or if that interest is outweighed by hardship to the employee and likely injury to the public. It provides confidentiality and trade-secret protection backstopped by the Arizona Uniform Trade Secrets Act (A.R.S. §§ 44-401 to 44-407), a continued-at-will-employment consideration recital, customer and employee non-solicitation drawn to the protectable-interest threshold, an optional non-compete sized to the actual footprint, confidentiality and non-solicits scoped so they do not operate as de-facto non-competes, a broadcast-employer screening recital for the one statutory ban (A.R.S. § 23-494), physician covenants drafted for Arizona's heightened public-interest scrutiny, and grammatically severable covenant drafting for Arizona's strict trim-only blue pencil, which strikes overbroad terms but never rewrites them. Drafted as a starting point for licensed counsel review. (OpenAgreements version 0.1.0, marked experimental by its authors.)

templates.title: Employee Restrictive Covenant Agreement
templates.summary: California-specific employee restrictive covenant agreement centered on confidentiality, trade secret protection, property return, and non-disparagement. templates.title: Employee Restrictive Covenant Agreement
templates.summary: Colorado-specific employee restrictive covenant agreement built for C.R.S. § 8-2-113: confidentiality and trade-secret protection with the statutory general-skills and protected-disclosure carve-outs, an employee non-solicitation covenant, a customer non-solicitation covenant gated on sixty percent of the highly compensated worker threshold ($78,008.40 for 2026), and an optional non-compete gated on the highly compensated worker threshold ($130,014 for 2026) and tied to trade-secret protection. Both earnings gates run at signing and at enforcement. The agreement flags the separate, signed 14-day advance-notice document the statute requires, excludes restrictive covenants for health-care providers under S.B. 25-083 with the patient-communication protections, keeps Colorado law and a Colorado forum for Colorado-based workers, and drafts each covenant within its enforceable scope rather than relying on discretionary judicial reformation. Drafted as a starting point for licensed counsel review. (OpenAgreements version 0.1.0, marked experimental by its authors.)

templates.title: Employee Restrictive Covenant Agreement
templates.summary: Connecticut-specific employee restrictive covenant agreement built for Connecticut's common-law reasonableness regime: there is no general Connecticut non-compete statute, so every post-employment restraint stands or falls on the five-factor common-law reasonableness test (partial and restricted as to time or place, fair protection of the employer, no undue hardship on the employee, no interference with the public interest, and no preclusion of the employee's occupation and livelihood). It provides confidentiality and trade-secret protection backstopped by the Connecticut Uniform Trade Secrets Act (Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 35-51 to 35-53), a continued-employment consideration recital drafted to prove the connection Connecticut's current consideration case law requires, customer and employee non-solicitation, an optional non-compete tied to a recognized protectable interest and sized to the employer's actual footprint, a physician clause reciting the § 20-14p one-year and fifteen-mile caps and the parallel §§ 20-12k / 20-101d caps for physician assistants and APRNs, statutory carve-outs excluding security-guard (§ 31-50a), broadcast-employee (§ 31-50b), and homemaker-companion / home-health (§§ 20-681, 20-683) restraints, and separable, tiered restraints drafted within their enforceable scope rather than in reliance on discretionary judicial narrowing, which Connecticut authority leaves unsettled. Drafted as a starting point for licensed counsel review. (OpenAgreements version 0.1.0, marked experimental by its authors.)

templates.title: Employee Restrictive Covenant Agreement
templates.summary: District of Columbia employee restrictive covenant agreement built for the Ban on Non-Compete Agreements Amendment Act of 2020 (D.C. Code §§ 32-581.01–.04b): confidentiality and trade-secret protection with the statutory information carve-out, an employee non-solicitation covenant, a customer non-solicitation covenant, and an optional non-compete confined to a highly compensated employee — one at or above the annually indexed minimum qualifying annual compensation ($162,164 for most employees in 2026; $270,274 for a medical specialist). The non-compete recites every § 32-581.03(a) validity gate: a stated functional scope and geographic limits, a term of no more than 365 calendar days from separation (730 for a medical specialist), and delivery of the covenant in writing at least 14 days in advance, with the prescribed statutory notice and the workplace-policy disclosure flagged as companion writings. For a covered employee below the threshold the covenant is banned and void as a matter of law, so the template omits it by default and never relies on judicial reformation to cure overbreadth. Drafted as a starting point for licensed counsel review. (OpenAgreements version 0.1.0, marked experimental by its authors.)

templates.title: Employee Restrictive Covenant Agreement
templates.summary: Delaware-specific employee restrictive covenant agreement built for Delaware's common-law reasonableness regime: there is no general Delaware non-compete statute, so every post-employment restraint stands or falls on the Court of Chancery's three-part review (reasonable in geographic scope and temporal duration, advancing a legitimate economic interest, and surviving a balancing of the equities), evaluated holistically across every dimension of the covenant. It provides confidentiality and trade-secret protection backstopped by the Delaware Uniform Trade Secrets Act (6 Del. C. §§ 2001-2007), a formation-stage consideration recital that names the value exchanged, customer and employee non-solicitation, an optional non-compete sized to identified legitimate interests, physician practice-covenant compliance that voids any practice restraint while preserving reasonably related damages (6 Del. C. § 2707), a home-inspector-trainee carve-out (24 Del. C. § 4109(d)), a Delaware choice-of-law anchor bounded by its statutory and conflict-of-law limits (6 Del. C. § 2708), and a draft-the-scope reformation posture the agreement does not rely on because recent decisions increasingly refuse to blue-pencil an overbroad covenant. Drafted as a starting point for licensed counsel review. (OpenAgreements version 0.1.0, marked experimental by its authors.)

templates.title: Employee Restrictive Covenant Agreement
templates.summary: Indiana-specific employee restrictive covenant agreement built for Indiana's common-law reasonableness regime: there is no general Indiana non-compete statute, so every post-employment restraint is a disfavored restraint construed strictly against the employer, which must first prove a legitimate protectable interest and then carry the burden of showing the restraint reasonable in time, activity, and geographic area. It provides confidentiality and trade-secret protection anchored to the Indiana Uniform Trade Secrets Act (Ind. Code § 24-2-3-2), customer and employee non-solicitation each tied to a protectable interest, and an optional non-compete sized to the employer's actual footprint. Because Indiana's blue pencil is a strict eraser that deletes but never rewrites, and a court cannot add terms even where the agreement purports to authorize it, the covenants are drafted as grammatically severable, independently reasonable units rather than in reliance on judicial reformation. The employee non-solicitation covenant is scoped to a protectable-interest-limited Covered Employees class rather than the workforce at large. A liquidated-damages provision is omitted by default because a sum grossly disproportionate to the loss is an unenforceable penalty. Physician covenants are governed by a layered statute stack keyed to execution date (House Enrolled Act 1004 (2020) content requirements including the reasonable-price buyout; the Senate Enrolled Act 7 (2023) primary care ban; the Senate Enrolled Act 475 (2025) physician-hospital ban). The agreement runs the statutory worker-protection gates before any covenant, states the without-cause severance-or-disclosed-compensation economics SB 170 requires for agreements entered into, amended, or renewed on or after July 1, 2026, excludes health care professionals, and — because Virginia courts do not rewrite an overbroad covenant — draws each covenant within its enforceable scope at the outset rather than relying on judicial reformation. Drafted as a starting point for licensed counsel review. (OpenAgreements version 0.1.0, marked experimental by its authors.)

templates.title: Employee Restrictive Covenant Agreement
templates.summary: Vermont-specific employee restrictive covenant agreement built for Vermont's common-law reasonableness regime: there is no general Vermont non-compete statute, so every post-employment restraint stands or falls on the common-law reasonableness test (enforcement is ordered unless the covenant is contrary to public policy, unnecessary for the employer's protection, or unnecessarily restrictive of the employee), framed by the courts through Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 188(1). It provides confidentiality and trade-secret protection backstopped by the Vermont Trade Secrets Act (9 V.S.A. §§ 4602-4603), a continued-at-will-employment consideration recital, customer and employee non-solicitation, an optional non-compete tied to identified protectable interests and sized to the actual footprint, an express tolling clause the drafting does not assume a court will supply, profession-specific exclusions for barbering/cosmetology trainees (26 V.S.A. § 281(c)) and lawyers (Vt. R. Prof. Conduct 5.6), healthcare-professional reasonableness scrutiny without assuming a statutory healthcare ban, and an ordinary severability clause the drafting treats as a backstop rather than a narrowing strategy because Vermont court narrowing is unsettled (the case law bars equitable rewriting of the time term while other decisions carry partial-enforcement dicta). Drafted as a starting point for licensed counsel review. (OpenAgreements version 0.1.0, marked experimental by its authors.)

templates.title: Employee Restrictive Covenant Agreement
templates.summary: Employee restrictive covenant agreement for Washington State, built for chapter 49.62 RCW as amended by SSB 5935 (effective 2024): confidentiality and trade-secret protection, customer and employee non-solicitation held to the statutory solicitation-only definition, and an optional non-compete gated on the inflation-adjusted earnings threshold ($126,858.83 for employees / $317,147.09 for independent contractors in 2026 per the Department of Labor & Industries), the at-hire written disclosure or post-hire independent consideration requirement, the eighteen-month duration presumption, and the layoff garden-leave-pay condition. Governing law, venue, and choice of law are locked to Washington for Washington-based workers under RCW 49.62.050, and the agreement flags the June 30, 2027 near-total ban under ESHB 1155 and the October 1, 2027 deadline for employers to make reasonable efforts to give written notice to affected employees and independent contractors that their non-competes are void and unenforceable. Because RCW 49.62.080(3) penalizes judicial reformation until ESHB 1155 deletes that penalty effective June 30, 2027, each covenant is drawn to the minimum the legitimate interest requires. Drafted as a starting point for licensed counsel review. (OpenAgreements version 0.1.0, marked experimental by its authors.)

templates.title: Employee Restrictive Covenant Agreement
templates.summary: Wisconsin-specific employee restrictive covenant agreement built for Wis. Stat. § 103.465, where a covenant is enforceable only if reasonably necessary to protect the employer, a five-factor reasonableness test governs every post-employment restraint, and an unreasonable restraint is void in full with no judicial blue-penciling. Confidentiality and trade-secret protection scoped to protectable information, customer and employee non-solicitation (the employee no-poach limited to actual working relationships), an optional non-compete drawn to the five-factor reasonableness standard, a consideration recital resting on genuine forbearance, no extension-during-breach tolling that would void the restraint, Wisconsin governing law rather than a foreign choice-of-law clause, and divisible covenants in place of reliance on reformation. Drafted as a starting point for licensed counsel review. (OpenAgreements version 0.1.0, marked experimental by its authors.)

templates.title: Employee Restrictive Covenant Agreement
templates.summary: West Virginia-specific employee restrictive covenant agreement built for West Virginia's common-law reasonableness regime with its facial-overbreadth void trap: there is no general West Virginia non-compete statute, so every post-employment restraint stands or falls on a two-stage common-law inquiry — the employer must first show an interest requiring protection, and the restraint is then reasonable only if it is no greater than required for the employer's protection, imposes no undue hardship on the employee, and is not injurious to the public. A covenant unreasonable on its face is utterly void with no partial enforcement, so the drafting does not rely on a savings or reformation clause to cure overbreadth. It provides confidentiality and trade-secret protection backstopped by the West Virginia Uniform Trade Secrets Act (W. Va. Code §§ 47-22-4, 47-22-7), a new-consideration recital for covenants signed after employment begins, customer restrictions drafted as true non-piracy provisions, employee non-solicitation, an optional non-compete tied to identified protectable interests and sized to the actual footprint, a sale-of-business acknowledgement under the lesser-scrutiny standard, and physician covenant limits capped at one year and thirty road miles with voidness on employer termination (W.
